extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of political theology, ecclesiastical law, and church–state relations (readers of 17th-century political philosophy)
extracted.subtask_description: Normative criteria and standards concerning who counts as a Christian martyr, the scope of apostles' and pastors' powers (preaching, teaching, baptizing, binding/loosing, excommunication), and the relation between ecclesiastical authority and civil sovereigns. Presented as a doctrinal/political-theological argument (17th-century context).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Martyr
rubrics_metrics.description: A Martyr is, (to give the true definition of the word) a Witnesse of the Resurrection of Jesus the Messiah; which none can be but those that conversed with him on earth, and saw him after he was risen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A witness must have seen what he testifieth or his testimony is not good; therefore properly martyrs are original disciples who saw Christ before and after his Resurrection. Others are at best 'second Martyrs'—martyrs of Christ's witnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single article deserving martyrdom
rubrics_metrics.description: ’Tis one Article onely, which to die for, meriteth so honorable a name; and that Article is this, that Jesus Is The Christ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To die for other tenets (those serving clergy ambition or profit) is not required and does not merit the honorable name of martyr; martyrdom is tied to bearing witness to the foundational article that Jesus is the Christ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calling requirement for true martyrdom
rubrics_metrics.description: None therefore can be a Martyr... that have not a warrant to preach Christ come in the flesh; that is to say, none, but such as are sent to the conversion of Infidels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those who have not been sent/called to preach are not obliged to suffer death for their private beliefs; being 'sent' (i.e., having a commission to convert unbelievers) is a necessary condition for primary martyr status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preaching confers ministerial, not magisterial, power
rubrics_metrics.description: Preachers therefore have not Magisteriall, but Ministeriall power: 'Bee not called Masters... for one is your Master, even Christ.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preaching is likened to proclamation by a crier or herald and does not give the preacher authority to command or coerce the congregation or to override civil law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching/preaching does not override civil obedience
rubrics_metrics.description: to teach out of the Old Testament that Jesus was Christ... is not to say, that men are bound after they beleeve it, to obey those that tell them so, against the laws, and commands of their Soveraigns; but that they shall doe wisely... with Obedience to their present Magistrates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The apostles' teaching should lead to patience and faith while maintaining obedience to existing civil magistrates; religious teaching is not a licence to disobey sovereign civil authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baptism signifies allegiance but does not create earthly authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Baptisme... is a signe of becomming a new man, and a loyall subject to that God... This... is not to constitute over us another authority, by which our externall actions are to be governed in this life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baptism declares reception into God's kingdom and promises to follow apostolic doctrine toward eternal life, but it does not institute a separate earthly authority that governs temporal actions while civil sovereignty endures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to remit/retain sins is conditional and outwardly judged
rubrics_metrics.description: By which words, is not granted an Authority to Forgive, or Retain Sinnes, simply and absolutely... but conditionally, to the Penitent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apostles/pastors judge repentance by outward marks (words and actions) only. They have no authority to discern true penitence of the heart; if repentance is feigned the absolution is void. The assembly (the Church) judges the cause, and sentence is pronounced by an apostle or pastor as prolocutor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excommunication aims to correct manners not to punish mere opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Excommunication in the time that Christian Religion was not authorized by the Civill Power, was used onely for a correction of manners, not of errours in opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excommunication's practical effect was to induce avoidance by the faithful and thereby correct scandalous conduct; it was not intended (nor justifiable in Scripture) to expel persons who hold non-fundamental doctrinal differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of excommunication depends on civil power
rubrics_metrics.description: The Use and Effect of Excommunication, whilest it was not yet strengthened with the Civill Power, was no more, than that they, who were not Excommunicate, were to avoid the company of them that were.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without civil enforcement, excommunication only entailed social avoidance by believers; it could not bar access to public places (which belong to commonwealth) unless civil authorities cooperated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for excommunication (moral offences)
rubrics_metrics.description: There Lyeth Excommunication for Injustice... And there lyeth Excommunication for a Scandalous Life, as (1 Cor. 5.) 'If any man that is called a Brother, be a Fornicator, or Covetous, or an Idolater, or a Drunkard, or an Extortioner...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excommunication is proper for grave immoral behaviour and scandal within the community; it is not warranted for disagreements that do not threaten the foundational article that Jesus is the Christ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection (haeretique) distinguished from excommunication
rubrics_metrics.description: An Haeretique... after the first and second admonition, reject. But to Reject (in this place) is not to Excommunicate the Man; But to Give Over Admonishing Him, To Let Him Alone...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scriptural injunctions to 'reject' or 'avoid foolish questions' are pastoral instructions to cease disputation, not authorization to cast faithful men out of the Church for non-fundamental doctrinal novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions required for a person to be liable to excommunication
rubrics_metrics.description: That a man be liable to Excommunication, there be many conditions requisite; as First, that he be a member of some Commonalty, that is to say, of some lawfull Assembly, that is to say, of some Christian Church, that hath power to judge of the cause for which hee is to bee Excommunicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excommunication presupposes membership in a community with judicial authority; where there is no community or no power to judge, there can be no excommunication. One church cannot validly excommunicate another as if it were a disciplinary act between unequal bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excommunication has no effect against sovereigns or subjects obeying their sovereign
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Sovereign Prince, or Assembly bee Excommunicate, the sentence is of no effect... Nor is the Excommunication of a Christian Subject, that obeyeth the laws of his own Soveraign... of any effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjects are bound by the law of nature to be in the company of their sovereign and cannot lawfully obey excommunication to the extent of disobeying their sovereign; true Christians who believe Jesus is the Christ cannot be harmed thereby.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family obligations not severed by parent/master excommunication
rubrics_metrics.description: If a mans Father, or Mother, or Master bee Excommunicate, yet are not the Children forbidden to keep them Company, nor to Eat with them...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excommunication should not impose impossible burdens (e.g., depriving dependents of food) nor authorize disobedience to parents or masters; the pastoral discipline must respect natural and civil obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreter of Scripture has no coercive authority without civil commission
rubrics_metrics.description: The Interpreter therefore of the Scripture... could be none: every one might beleeve, or not beleeve, according as the Allegations seemed to himself?... For the Conversion of the Gentiles, there was no use of alledging the Scriptures... The Apostles therefore laboured by Reason to confute their Idolatry...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When converts do not already accept a written canon, an interpreter who lacks legal commission cannot bind the people's assent; arguing from Scriptures makes the audience judge the proofs themselves. Only when a pastor or civil sovereign authorizes an interpretation does it take on coercive force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to make Scripture law belongs to civil sovereigns
rubrics_metrics.description: The question therefore here, is of the Power to make the Scriptures (which are the Rules of Christian Faith) Laws... The Canonizing, or making of the Scripture Law, belonged to the Civill Soveraign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: the Ten Commandments (first table) and the Judicial and Levitical laws became laws by virtue of Moses as civil sovereign; canonical force as law depends on civil promulgation/recognition and the consent/bond between sovereign and people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ten Commandments: first table concerns sovereignty, second table concerns duties between persons
rubrics_metrics.description: The first containeth the law of Soveraignty... The second Table containeth the Duty of one man towards another... The question now is, Who it was that gave to these written Tables theobligatory force of Lawes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some parts of scripture (e.g., second table) correspond to natural law binding on all; other parts (first table) were particular to Israel and became binding as civil law via acceptance of Moses' leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial and Levitical law promulgated by civil sovereign (Moses)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Judiciall Law... and the Leviticall Law... were all delivered to them by Moses onely; and therefore also became Lawes, by vertue of the same promise of obedience to Moses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive prescriptions concerning administration of justice and priestly rites were instituted as law by the civil authority exercising sovereignty (Moses/High Priests); the canonization function is thus tied to civil office.
